text:
josh-people: Quick Q from APAC eng  Lees region has a statutory public holiday on Dec 26 (Boxing Day observed) but our company year-end blackout is Dec 20Dec 31. Lee is asking if they can take that day as a company-observed holiday, use PTO, or we need coverage.

lee-apac-eng: Manager ping 449 Im in Singapore office. Boxing Day is observed on 12/26 here. I assume Redwood only observes US federal holidays, so Id need to use PTO or take it unpaid. Can we mark it as local observed holiday?

anya-hrbp: Policy recap: Redwood bank of company holidays is global but localized based on office region. For employees based in an APAC office, statutory local holidays are observed as company holidays if they are part of the office holiday calendar. If you're remote in APAC but listed as US payroll, it's trickier. What's Lees payroll location?

lee-apac-eng: On Singapore payroll (local entity). Manager confirmed in DM.

sam-usa-eng: Manager note: Team has a sprint freeze Dec 22Dec 29 so coverage is light. If Lee is off on 12/26 we need someone to handle an on-call handover that day. Happy to swap shifts.

josh-people: Good: since Lee is on Singapore payroll, 12/26 should be a company holiday for them and not count against PTO. That said, because our global console marks year-end blackout 12/2012/31 for critical coverage, any coverage gaps still need manager + People Ops visibility. For Singapore-holiday employees the blackout doesn't force using PTO, but we still request documented coverage plan if the role is critical.

anya-hrbp: Operational steps: 1) Manager to confirm coverage plan in this thread (who does handover / which teammate covers). 2) People Ops will mark 12/26 as a localized company holiday in HRIS for Lee so it won't deduct PTO. 3) If teammates swap shifts (US covering APAC hours), payroll needs a comp-day record for the coverer.

payroll-bot: If a US teammate covers Lees shift and wants a comp-day, payroll accepts CSV: 

```
worker_id, reason, comp_date, pay_code
33421, "cover APAC Boxing Day (12/26) for Lee", 2027-01-04, COMP-DAY
```

Send to payroll@redwood.com and cc people-ops. Comp-days for cross-region coverage are coded as COMP-DAY and can be used within the next quarter.

sam-usa-eng: I can cover the handover window on 12/26. Will that show as comp-day in my balance automatically or do I need to file?

josh-people: You'll need a quick confirmation email from your manager indicating you covered Lees shift and the preferred comp_date. Then payroll CSV as above. We recommend comp_date within Q1 2027.

lee-apac-eng: Thanks all. Manager confirmed (DM & calendar invite). Can People Ops mark 12/26 as Singapore holiday in HRIS so it doesn't count as PTO?

anya-hrbp: Yes. I'll file HR ticket and mark localized holiday. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/HR-2133. Also noting the coverage: Sam will cover 12/26 handover; manager will confirm in email and Sam will file payroll CSV for comp-day.

calendar-bot: Reminder: Year-end blackout 2026-12-20 to 2026-12-31. Local statutory holidays for regional payrolls do not automatically bypass blackout; exceptions for coverage must be documented.

josh-people: Closing: People Ops will update HRIS for Lee and ping payroll once Sam's manager email + CSV arrives. Sam: please confirm in thread once you send payroll email so we have written record. :thumbsup: 

sam-usa-eng: Confirmed 44D I'll email payroll today and cc you.
